tips.comment: Kilteel can go well for the Dunlop yard. Kilteel was third at this track last time out in October and is wearing a hood for the first time today. The trainer is in very good form.

This looks like a weak race, and Bantz stands out. He boasts the best speed ratings in the field, indicating he should have the edge. Kaiya Fraser's record on Bantz is impressive, with only one non-placing in four rides, including a victory. While this is only his second attempt at this distance, his strong finish last time suggests he will handle it well. The previous mile attempt is easily forgiven, as there was no apparent reason for the poor performance.

Herkeios was below par at Wolverhampton last time but had previously run well in a pair of solid handicaps, including a close second at Southwell off this same mark of 65. That effort reads well in the context of this weaker contest. He’s proven over the trip, handles Tapeta, and returns to a straight mile which could play to his strengths. If he can recapture that Southwell form, he looks a leading player here and the early double-figure odds offer fair value.
Nicely bred and has the form to feature in what looks like a winnable race. Has run well in a couple of useful maidens on turf.

La Botte ran a lot better than the market expected on debut at Kempton, staying on nicely for third over 7f. That looked a fair race and he shaped like one who’d come on plenty for it. Up to a mile now and with that experience under his belt, he should be sharper. Wouldn’t be surprised to see him go very close.
Still a maiden after 24 outings, but has been running well as of late over C/D as well. This could finally be the day it breaks its maiden tag.
€170,000 Wootton Bassett colt. Amo Racing owned and wouldn't dismiss despite the big price. Yard scores a profit for punters around this venue.

A speculative selection - but Grizzieblanca looks too big a price. She fluffed the start last time and put in no sort of show. She cost 47k and should not be written off on that run alone. The trainer drops her in trip tonight and with a featherweight burden of 8-10 she could run into a place. Either way, one to keep an eye on.

Tuco Salamanca has shown some encouraging signs in his recent runs. He has been settling well early on and then picking up the pace in the latter stages which suits Newcastle’s track conditions perfectly.

Saxonia looks like a strong prospect based on her recent form and the way she handles similar conditions. Her previous runs show she settles well early and then has a steady finish that can challenge the leaders in a competitive field. The current track conditions favor her running style and make her a horse worth considering today.
3rd to Tuco Salamanca 15 days ago when he gave 2 lbs, now 3 lbs better off. Improving since yard switch and now brought back slightly in trip, which should suit.

Oriental Prince is in great form and looks poised to lead the field. His strong early pace and powerful finishing ability have impressed, and today’s track conditions perfectly suit his running style.

This horse has been beaten a neck in his 2 recent runs over c&d off a 1lb lower mark. He traded very short odds on both occasions and was particularly unlucky in one of those races where Jonny Peate was on board and travelling like a dream before being hampered at a crucial time. That was his only ride on the horse and I like his booking here to make amends for that defeat. Looks sure to go very close here.
Comes here off a falling mark and has had excuses, having been given too much to do in a couple of his races. But now his mark is down to a career low of 62, has a decent each-way chance.
Three-time C&D winner. Exposed but a good strike rate. Has been in good form for a while and looks capable of getting involved.

Rebecca's Girl deserves another win just for her consistency! She's been running really well over 6 and 7 furlongs over the past few months and can give another account today. Second last time out here over 6 furlongs she steps back up to her ideal 7 and should go close.

The six furlongs latest would have been too short. Now back up to what looks like his ideal trip after finishing well last time. The trainer has already had a winner this month, so the string may be further forward than usual.
WYVERN just looks a big price for a horse that very nearly won earlier in the week. Grade and distance shouldn't be a problem despite changes to both and could win it from here.

Race 7 at Newcastle today is the Weekly Free Bets With BetMGM Extra Handicap (Class 5) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,421 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Starliner from the L. A. Perratt yard, and will be ridden by Tommie Jakes. This son of Showcasing is a two-time winner and has been knocking on the door in recent runs. Rates a danger on form and cannot be ignored here.
This gelding's yard is in flying form, and the horse himself won off a 2lb lower mark last week. Everything looks set for the follow-up, and the price is very appealing.

Kings School is in excellent form and shows all the signs of being a real contender. His recent performances have been impressive, with a strong early pace followed by a powerful finish that has often put him ahead of the field. Today’s conditions are ideal for his running style, and he has the potential to outrun his odds.

Lightly raced 4yo. Just average on the AW this winter but he has been racing in higher grade races. Just two career turf runs. Beaten just 3L when last seen on grass, last autumn, and he now has a 16lb lower mark. Strong jockey booking for this amateur riders' handicap.

Just five career runs for the 3yo. He was a close runner-up in his two final starts last year, strong maiden form. Back from a 6 month break with an AW maiden win three weeks ago, which should set him up for his handicap debut. Decent opening mark - top yard.

He's coming off a 7 month break but the 5yo won a class 2, 18 runner handicap on his return last year - 7lb lower mark now after some below par efforts in the second half of last year. Yard in good shape and can be a player in this class 3 handicap.

This is the first time ever that the excellent Pam Sly has booked Oisin Murphy and this one could go very well for her on debut for the stable. There's no doubt that this Kingman gelding has the form in the book to go very close here if fit enough, and the trainer has her string in good order at the moment. The horse has been placed off 91 twice in his 3 runs in this class and is down to 86 now so the 5yos chance is there for everyone to see with conditions to suit.

The 4yo was totally unsuited by the quick ground in Bahrain in two recent runs, but his fitness should be fine. He ran well last autumn on slower turf ground, good RPR ratings posted. With the jockey's claim he's effectively 10lb better off from his final start last year.
Has visited Doncaster twice on decent ground and has finished 2nd over this trip and last year won over a mile from 1lb lower. Looks a cracking each way price and should be strong at the finish.
French import. Four UK runs for the 4yo last year, a couple of decent efforts in higher grade handicaps than this one. Three AW runs last month will have him fit. On an attractive mark.

A three time course and distance winner which counts for plenty here was last seen at Southwell 30 days ago where making his return run after a 111 days break where finishing 2nd/5 and was only just denied the win by a nose now with that run under his belt returning to a suitable turf track here he can go a place better this time out and arrives here in top nick and in very good heart so he must be taken very seriously as he looks poised to strike here jockey Warren Fentiman takes of a very valuable looking 5lb which only enhances his good looking claims here trainer Phillip Mcbride has an impressive £110.90 profit to a £1 level stake when having just the one runner at a fleeting meeting amd Onemorenomore is more than capable of enhancing that statistic further merits serious consideration
Looks like an unexposed horse that made a good start in handicap races when coming in first last time out. Up 7lb, but plenty more to come.

Sits 2 lbs below the mark he ran off in this race last season. Coming into this race with a bit to prove at present. He's evidently not as good as he once was. To be fair, he's almost a teenager now, so it's to be expected. He ran a cracker in this event last season. Beaten just 1/2 L behind the winner Sam Brown. A solid effort trying to give 8 lbs in weight to the winner. I felt he ran a great race over CD on reappearance this season behind stablemate Chianti Classico. Beaten just 7 L back in 4th place. This is clearly his favourite track. He boasts plenty of useful form here, including a 2nd place finish behind Fakir d'Oudairies in the 2022 running of the Betfair Chase. He goes well fresh, which bodes well. He can go well on good or soft ground, so the weather won't stop him. If he runs his usual race, that would see him thereabouts in this very winnable race.
